test_cases.description: Verify that the AfterUserCreateFunc type is exported from the apikit package with the correct signature.
preconditions: apikit package is compiled from the local replace path ../apikit
No hook has been registered on the server
test_cases.input: Inspect the apikit package for the exported type AfterUserCreateFunc
test_cases.expected: AfterUserCreateFunc is a public type with signature func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, userID, username, email string) error; the package compiles without error
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: var fn apikit.AfterUserCreateFunc = func(ctx, tx, userID, username, email) error { return nil }; assert fn != nil AND typeof(fn) == apikit.AfterUserCreateFunc

test_cases.description: Verify that OnAfterUserCreate stores the provided hook function on the server and replaces any previous registration.
preconditions: apikit Server is instantiated via NewServer with a valid Config and HealthChecker
No hook is registered initially
test_cases.input: Call server.OnAfterUserCreate(hookFn) with a non-nil AfterUserCreateFunc
test_cases.expected: The server stores hookFn internally; a subsequent call with a different hookFn2 replaces hookFn such that only hookFn2 is called during user creation
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: callCount1 := 0; callCount2 := 0; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...) { callCount1++ }); server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...) { callCount2++ }); simulateUserCreate(server); assert callCount1 == 0 AND callCount2 == 1

test_cases.description: Verify that user creation proceeds normally without calling any hook when no hook has been registered.
preconditions: apikit Server is instantiated
No OnAfterUserCreate has been called
Database is initialised with the users table
test_cases.input: Trigger user creation (OAuth new-user branch or admin createUser) with no registered hook
test_cases.expected: User row is inserted successfully; no panic or error occurs; HTTP 201 (admin) or redirect (OAuth) is returned
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: server := NewServer(cfg, checker); MountHandlers(server, db); result := createUserViaAdmin(server, {username:'alice', email:'alice@example.com'}); assert result.statusCode == 201 AND userExistsInDB('alice') == true

test_cases.description: Verify that registering a second hook replaces the first and only the second hook is called during user creation.
preconditions: apikit Server is instantiated
Database is initialised
test_cases.input: Call OnAfterUserCreate twice with distinct functions hookA and hookB, then trigger user creation
test_cases.expected: hookA is never called; hookB is called exactly once with correct parameters
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: calledA := false; calledB := false; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ calledA = true; return nil }); server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ calledB = true; return nil }); triggerNewUserCreation(server); assert calledA == false AND calledB == true

test_cases.description: Verify that a hook registered before MountHandlers is invoked in both the OAuth new-user branch and the admin createUser handler.
preconditions: apikit Server is instantiated
Hook is registered via OnAfterUserCreate before MountHandlers is called
Database has users and orgs tables
test_cases.input: Register hook, call MountHandlers, then trigger (1) OAuth new-user callback and (2) admin user creation
test_cases.expected: Hook is called exactly once in each scenario; hook receives the correct userID, username, and email in both cases
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: invokedPaths := []; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(ctx, tx, id, name, email){ invokedPaths.append(name); return nil }); server.MountHandlers(db); triggerOAuthNewUser(server, 'bob'); triggerAdminCreateUser(server, 'carol'); assert invokedPaths == ['bob', 'carol']

test_cases.description: Verify that the AfterUserCreateFunc hook is called with the active transaction and new user details after a new user INSERT during OAuth callback.
preconditions: apikit Server has hook registered via OnAfterUserCreate before MountHandlers
Database has users table; no existing user row for the test user
OAuth provider mock returns a new user identity
test_cases.input: Simulate OAuth callback for a new user 'dave' with email 'dave@example.com'
test_cases.expected: Hook is called with non-nil *sql.Tx, userID matching the inserted row, username='dave', email='dave@example.com'; hook is called before transaction commit
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: capturedArgs := nil; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(ctx, tx, id, name, email){ capturedArgs = {tx, id, name, email}; return nil }); simulateOAuthCallback(server, newUser={name:'dave', email:'dave@example.com'}); assert capturedArgs.tx != nil AND capturedArgs.name == 'dave' AND capturedArgs.email == 'dave@example.com' AND userExistsInDB('dave')

test_cases.description: Verify that a non-nil error from the hook during OAuth callback rolls back the transaction and returns HTTP 500.
preconditions: apikit Server has hook registered that always returns errors.New('hook failed')
Database has users table; no existing user row for the test user
OAuth provider mock returns a new user identity
test_cases.input: Simulate OAuth callback for a new user 'eve'
test_cases.expected: HTTP 500 response returned to OAuth caller; no user row for 'eve' exists in the database; no partial org or other rows created
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(ctx, tx, id, name, email){ return errors.New('hook failed') }); response := simulateOAuthCallback(server, {name:'eve'}); assert response.statusCode == 500 AND userExistsInDB('eve') == false

test_cases.description: Verify that the hook is NOT called when the OAuth callback identifies a returning (existing) user.
preconditions: apikit Server has hook registered
Database has an existing user row for user 'frank'
OAuth provider mock returns identity matching 'frank'
test_cases.input: Simulate OAuth callback for returning user 'frank'
test_cases.expected: Hook is never called; user row is not duplicated; normal login flow completes successfully
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: hookCallCount := 0; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ hookCallCount++; return nil }); simulateOAuthCallback(server, existingUser={name:'frank'}); assert hookCallCount == 0

test_cases.description: Verify that the createUser handler wraps the user INSERT and hook call in a database transaction.
preconditions: apikit Server has hook registered
Database is accessible with users table
test_cases.input: Call admin createUser endpoint with valid user payload
test_cases.expected: The user INSERT and hook call execute within the same *sql.Tx; the hook receives a non-nil *sql.Tx that matches the one used for the user INSERT
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: receivedTx := nil; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(ctx, tx, id, name, email){ receivedTx = tx; return nil }); triggerAdminCreateUser(server, {username:'grace'}); assert receivedTx != nil AND typeof(receivedTx) == *sql.Tx AND userExistsInDB('grace')

test_cases.description: Verify that the hook is called with correct user details after a successful user INSERT inside the admin createUser transaction.
preconditions: apikit Server with hook registered before MountHandlers
Database has users table; no existing user 'henry'
test_cases.input: POST to admin user creation endpoint with {username:'henry', email:'henry@example.com'}
test_cases.expected: Hook is called with userID matching the inserted row, username='henry', email='henry@example.com', and a non-nil *sql.Tx
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: captured := nil; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(ctx, tx, id, name, email){ captured = {id, name, email} }); triggerAdminCreateUser({username:'henry', email:'henry@example.com'}); assert captured.name == 'henry' AND captured.email == 'henry@example.com' AND captured.id != ''

test_cases.description: Verify that a hook error during admin user creation rolls back the transaction and returns HTTP 500.
preconditions: apikit Server has hook registered that returns errors.New('hook error')
Database has users table; no existing user 'ivan'
test_cases.input: POST to admin user creation endpoint with {username:'ivan'}
test_cases.expected: HTTP 500 response; no user row for 'ivan' in the database; no partial state written
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ return errors.New('hook error') }); response := triggerAdminCreateUser({username:'ivan'}); assert response.statusCode == 500 AND userExistsInDB('ivan') == false

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: columns := db.query('PRAGMA table_info(orgs)'); ownerCol := columns.find(name='owner_id'); assert ownerCol != nil AND ownerCol.type == 'TEXT' AND ownerCol.notnull == 0

test_cases.description: Verify that the admin org creation endpoint (POST /orgs) accepts an optional owner_id field and stores it.

Database has orgs table with owner_id column

test_cases.description: Verify that the slug sanitizer lowercases the entire username before further processing.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook slug sanitizer function is available
test_cases.input: username = 'Alice'
test_cases.expected: Sanitized slug is 'alice' (all lowercase)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: slug := sanitizeSlug('Alice', userID='uid-001'); assert slug == 'alice'

test_cases.description: Verify that characters not in [a-z0-9_-] are replaced with hyphens during slug sanitization.
preconditions: Hub slug sanitizer function is available
test_cases.input: username = 'alice@example'
test_cases.expected: Sanitized slug has '@' replaced with '-', yielding 'alice-example'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: slug := sanitizeSlug('alice@example', userID='uid-001'); assert slug == 'alice-example'

test_cases.description: Verify that consecutive hyphens are collapsed into a single hyphen during sanitization.
preconditions: Hub slug sanitizer function is available
test_cases.input: username = 'alice--bob'
test_cases.expected: Sanitized slug is 'alice-bob'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: slug := sanitizeSlug('alice--bob', userID='uid-001'); assert slug == 'alice-bob'

test_cases.description: Verify that leading and trailing hyphens and underscores are trimmed from the sanitized slug.
preconditions: Hub slug sanitizer function is available
test_cases.input: username = '-alice_'
test_cases.expected: Sanitized slug is 'alice' (leading hyphen and trailing underscore trimmed)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: slug := sanitizeSlug('-alice_', userID='uid-001'); assert slug == 'alice'

test_cases.description: Verify that a sanitized slug starting with a digit gets the 'u-' prefix prepended.
preconditions: Hub slug sanitizer function is available
test_cases.input: username = '42alice'
test_cases.expected: Sanitized slug is 'u-42alice' (digit-leading slug gets 'u-' prefix)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: slug := sanitizeSlug('42alice', userID='uid-001'); assert slug starts with 'u-' AND slug == 'u-42alice'

test_cases.description: Verify that when the sanitized slug is shorter than 2 characters, the fallback u-<first 8 chars of userID> is used.
preconditions: Hub slug sanitizer function is available
test_cases.input: username = 'a', userID = 'abcdefgh-1234'
test_cases.expected: Sanitized slug is 'u-abcdefgh' (fallback: 'u-' + first 8 chars of userID='abcdefgh')
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: slug := sanitizeSlug('a', userID='abcdefgh-1234'); assert slug == 'u-abcdefgh'

test_cases.description: Verify that slug collision resolution appends -1, -2, etc. until a unique slug is found.
preconditions: SQLite database with orgs table containing rows with slugs 'alice' and 'alice-1'
Hub personal org hook is available and connected to the database
test_cases.input: Hook called with username='alice', userID='user-001'; orgs table already has slugs 'alice' and 'alice-1'
test_cases.expected: Hook inserts org with slug 'alice-2'; no error returned
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: tx := beginTx(db); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-001', 'alice', 'alice@test.com'); tx.commit(); assert err == nil; dbRow := db.query('SELECT slug FROM orgs WHERE owner_id=?', 'user-001'); assert dbRow.slug == 'alice-2'

test_cases.description: Verify that when all 10 slug suffix attempts collide, the hook returns an error causing transaction rollback and HTTP 500.
preconditions: SQLite database with orgs table containing slugs 'alice', 'alice-1' through 'alice-10'
Hub personal org hook is available
test_cases.input: Hook called with username='alice', userID='user-002'; orgs table has 'alice', 'alice-1', ..., 'alice-10'
test_cases.expected: Hook returns a non-nil error; no new org row is inserted; caller receives HTTP 500 when wired through the handler
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: tx := beginTx(db); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-002', 'alice', 'e@test.com'); assert err != nil; tx.rollback(); orgCount := db.query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orgs WHERE owner_id=?', 'user-002'); assert orgCount == 0

test_cases.description: Verify that when the candidate slug does not collide, it is used immediately without any suffix.
preconditions: SQLite database with orgs table containing no row with slug 'newuser'
Hub personal org hook is available
test_cases.input: Hook called with username='newuser', userID='user-003'
test_cases.expected: Hook inserts org with slug exactly 'newuser'; no suffix appended
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: tx := beginTx(db); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-003', 'newuser', 'n@test.com'); tx.commit(); assert err == nil; dbRow := db.query('SELECT slug FROM orgs WHERE owner_id=?', 'user-003'); assert dbRow.slug == 'newuser'

test_cases.description: Verify that the hub hook inserts an orgs row with all required fields correctly populated.
preconditions: SQLite database with orgs table including owner_id column; no existing org for 'julia'
Hub personal org hook available
test_cases.input: Hook called with username='Julia', email='julia@example.com', userID='user-julia-001'
test_cases.expected: orgs row inserted with: id=non-empty UUID, name='Julia' (original username), slug='julia' (sanitized), url='', owner_id='user-julia-001', status='active', created_at and updated_at in RFC 3339 format
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: tx := beginTx(db); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-julia-001', 'Julia', 'julia@example.com'); tx.commit(); row := db.query('SELECT * FROM orgs WHERE owner_id=?', 'user-julia-001'); assert row.id != '' AND row.name == 'Julia' AND row.slug == 'julia' AND row.url == '' AND row.owner_id == 'user-julia-001' AND row.status == 'active' AND isRFC3339(row.created_at) AND isRFC3339(row.updated_at)

test_cases.description: Verify that the hub hook inserts an org_members row linking the new user to the new org.
preconditions: SQLite database with orgs and org_members tables; no existing org for 'karl'
Hub personal org hook available
test_cases.input: Hook called with username='karl', userID='user-karl-001'
test_cases.expected: org_members row inserted with org_id matching the new org's id, user_id='user-karl-001', and created_at in RFC 3339 format
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: tx := beginTx(db); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-karl-001', 'karl', 'k@test.com'); tx.commit(); orgRow := db.query('SELECT id FROM orgs WHERE owner_id=?', 'user-karl-001'); memberRow := db.query('SELECT * FROM org_members WHERE user_id=?', 'user-karl-001'); assert memberRow.org_id == orgRow.id AND memberRow.user_id == 'user-karl-001' AND isRFC3339(memberRow.created_at)

test_cases.description: Verify that the hook performs all INSERT statements using the *sql.Tx passed to it, not a separate connection.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook available
Database is accessible
test_cases.input: Hook called with a spy transaction wrapper that records SQL statements executed on it
test_cases.expected: All INSERT statements (orgs and org_members) are executed on the passed *sql.Tx; no direct database connection is used for inserts
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: txSpy := newSpyTx(realTx); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, txSpy, 'user-100', 'luna', 'l@test.com'); assert txSpy.insertCount == 2 AND txSpy.statements contains 'INSERT INTO orgs' AND txSpy.statements contains 'INSERT INTO org_members'

test_cases.description: Verify that workspace creation without org_id auto-assigns the user's personal org id as the workspace org_id.

afc CLI is configured with valid auth token

test_cases.description: Verify that the hub server initialization registers the personal org hook before calling MountWorkspaceHandlers.
preconditions: Hub server initialization code is inspectable
apikit Server instance is available
test_cases.input: Trace hub server startup sequence
test_cases.expected: OnAfterUserCreate is called with the personal org hook function before MountWorkspaceHandlers (which calls MountHandlers internally); hook is active when handlers are wired
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: callOrder := []; server.OnAfterUserCreate = wrapper(real, func(){ callOrder.append('OnAfterUserCreate') }); MountWorkspaceHandlers = wrapper(real, func(){ callOrder.append('MountWorkspaceHandlers') }); initHubServer(); assert callOrder.indexOf('OnAfterUserCreate') < callOrder.indexOf('MountWorkspaceHandlers')

test_cases.description: Verify that apikit Server uses the hook reference captured at MountHandlers call time; hooks registered after MountHandlers are not guaranteed to be invoked.
preconditions: apikit Server instantiated
First hook (hookA) registered before MountHandlers
MountHandlers is called
Second hook (hookB) registered after MountHandlers
test_cases.input: Register hookA, call MountHandlers, register hookB, then trigger a new user creation
test_cases.expected: hookA is called (or hookB, depending on implementation); the system does not panic; the PRD-defined behavior is that hooks after MountHandlers are not guaranteed — test documents that hookB may or may not be invoked but no panic occurs
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: calledA := false; calledB := false; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ calledA = true }); server.MountHandlers(db); server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ calledB = true }); assert doesNotPanic(func(){ triggerNewUserCreation(server) }); // At least one hook fires without error assert calledA OR calledB

property_tests.description: For any user creation attempt, after the operation completes, either both the user row and a personal org row exist (with matching owner_id) or neither exists — no partial state is possible.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random (username, email) pairs for both OAuth and admin creation paths; randomly inject hook failures for approximately 50% of attempts
property_tests.invariant_check: after each attempt: (userExistsInDB(username) AND orgExistsForUser(userID)) OR (NOT userExistsInDB(username) AND NOT orgExistsForUser(userID)); never assert exactly one of the pair exists

property_tests.description: For any call to the hub personal org hook, the slug written to the orgs table does not duplicate any pre-existing slug in the table.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate arbitrary sets of pre-existing org slugs (0 to 15 slugs) and arbitrary usernames; run the hook against each combination
property_tests.invariant_check: after hook completes without error: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orgs WHERE slug = insertedSlug == 1 (no duplicate); if hook returns error due to cap exceeded, no new org row exists

property_tests.description: For any workspace creation request via POST /api/v1/workspaces, the persisted workspace row always has a non-null org_id.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate workspace creation requests with and without org_id field for users with and without personal orgs
property_tests.invariant_check: if response.statusCode == 201: SELECT org_id FROM workspaces WHERE id=workspaceID returns a non-null, non-empty value; if response.statusCode != 201: no workspace row exists for that slug

property_tests.description: The AfterUserCreateFunc hook is invoked exactly once per new-user INSERT and never for returning users.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate sequences of OAuth callbacks with a mix of new users (not in DB) and returning users (already in DB); track hook invocation count per callback
property_tests.invariant_check: for each callback: if user was new → hookInvocationCount for that user == 1; if user was returning → hookInvocationCount for that user == 0; total hook invocations == number of genuinely new users in the sequence

property_tests.description: For any username string, the slug sanitizer always produces a result that matches the validateSlug regex ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*[a-z0-9]$ (minimum 2 chars).
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate arbitrary Unicode strings as usernames (length 0 to 200); generate arbitrary userID strings (length 8 to 36)
property_tests.invariant_check: slug := sanitizeSlug(username, userID); assert slug matches regex '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*[a-z0-9]$' AND len(slug) >= 2; assert validateSlug(slug) returns nil error

property_tests.description: The slug collision retry loop always terminates after at most 10 iterations, regardless of how many slugs exist in the orgs table.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate orgs tables with 0 to 20 pre-existing slugs matching the candidate pattern (base, base-1 through base-20); instrument the loop iteration counter
property_tests.invariant_check: iterationCount := countLoopIterations(hubOrgHook, ...); assert iterationCount <= 10; if all 10 collide → err != nil; if unique found at iteration k ≤ 10 → err == nil AND slug is unique

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that calling OnAfterUserCreate after MountHandlers does not panic or error, even if behavior is undefined.
preconditions: apikit Server instantiated and MountHandlers already called
edge_case_tests.input: Call server.OnAfterUserCreate(hookFn) after MountHandlers has returned
edge_case_tests.expected: No panic; no error returned; the call completes silently (hook may or may not be wired)
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: server.MountHandlers(db); assert doesNotPanic(func(){ server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...) error { return nil }) })

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that when the OAuth request context is cancelled while the hook executes, the transaction rolls back and HTTP 500 is returned.
preconditions: apikit Server with a hook that blocks until context is cancelled
Database has users table; no existing user 'timeout-user'
edge_case_tests.input: Simulate OAuth callback for new user 'timeout-user' with a context that is cancelled after 10ms
edge_case_tests.expected: Hook's database operations fail with a context error; hook returns non-nil error; transaction rolls back; HTTP 500 returned; no user row for 'timeout-user' exists
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: ctx, cancel := contextWithTimeout(10ms); server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(ctx, tx, id, name, email){ sleep(100ms); return ctx.Err() }); response := simulateOAuthCallback(server, ctx, {name:'timeout-user'}); assert response.statusCode == 500 AND userExistsInDB('timeout-user') == false

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that when a transaction cannot be started in createUser, HTTP 500 is returned without any INSERT attempted.
preconditions: apikit Server with hook registered
Database connection is unavailable or returns error on Begin()
edge_case_tests.input: POST to admin user creation endpoint with valid payload while database is unavailable
edge_case_tests.expected: HTTP 500 returned; no user row created; no org row created; hook is never called
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: hookCalled := false; server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ hookCalled = true; return nil }); db.simulateBeginError(); response := triggerAdminCreateUser({username:'nostart'}); assert response.statusCode == 500 AND hookCalled == false AND userExistsInDB('nostart') == false

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that a fatal hook or transaction error in createUser is propagated as HTTP 500 without calling os.Exit or panic from library code.
preconditions: apikit Server used as a library (not CLI entrypoint)
Hook registered that returns a non-nil error simulating a fatal condition
edge_case_tests.input: Trigger admin user creation; hook returns errors.New('fatal hook error')
edge_case_tests.expected: HTTP 500 response returned to caller; no panic or os.Exit is invoked; process continues running
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: server.OnAfterUserCreate(func(...){ return errors.New('fatal hook error') }); assert doesNotPanic(func(){ response := triggerAdminCreateUser({username:'panic-test'}); assert response.statusCode == 500 })

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that a database error during slug uniqueness query causes the hook to return an error and roll back the transaction.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook available
Database transaction spy configured to return an error on the slug SELECT query
edge_case_tests.input: Hook called; SELECT slug uniqueness query against orgs returns a database error
edge_case_tests.expected: Hook returns a non-nil error; transaction is rolled back; caller receives HTTP 500; no org or org_members row created
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: tx := faultyTx(errorOn='SELECT.*FROM orgs WHERE slug'); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-200', 'queryerr', 'q@test.com'); assert err != nil; orgCount := db.query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orgs WHERE owner_id=?', 'user-200'); assert orgCount == 0

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that the slug collision retry loop is capped at exactly 10 iterations regardless of table state.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook slug collision loop logic is instrumentable
Database orgs table has all possible slugs for 'testslug' through 'testslug-20' to ensure all attempts would collide
edge_case_tests.input: Hook called with a slug that collides on every attempt; loop iteration counter is instrumented
edge_case_tests.expected: Loop executes exactly 10 iterations and then returns an error; iteration count never exceeds 10
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: iterationCount := 0; wrappedSlugCheck := func(slug){ iterationCount++; return slugExistsAlways(slug) }; err := hubOrgHookWithCustomCheck(ctx, tx, 'user-300', 'testslug', 't@test.com', wrappedSlugCheck); assert err != nil AND iterationCount == 10

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that if the orgs INSERT fails, the hook returns an error and rolls back all inserts including the user row.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook available
Transaction configured to fail on INSERT INTO orgs (e.g., simulated constraint violation)
edge_case_tests.input: Hook called; orgs INSERT returns a constraint violation error
edge_case_tests.expected: Hook returns non-nil error; transaction rolls back; no user, org, or org_members rows remain in the database
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: tx := faultyTx(errorOn='INSERT INTO orgs'); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-400', 'failorg', 'f@test.com'); assert err != nil; tx.rollback(); assert orgExistsForUser('user-400') == false

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that if org_members INSERT fails after orgs INSERT succeeds, the hook returns an error and rolls back all inserts.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook available
Transaction configured to succeed on INSERT INTO orgs but fail on INSERT INTO org_members
edge_case_tests.input: Hook called; org_members INSERT returns error after orgs row is inserted within the transaction
edge_case_tests.expected: Hook returns non-nil error; transaction rolls back; no user, org, or org_members rows remain
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: tx := faultyTx(errorOn='INSERT INTO org_members'); err := hubOrgHook(ctx, tx, 'user-401', 'failmember', 'fm@test.com'); assert err != nil; tx.rollback(); assert orgExistsForUser('user-401') == false AND memberExistsForUser('user-401') == false

edge_case_tests.description: Verify that if UUID generation for the new org id fails, the hook returns an error immediately without performing any INSERT.
preconditions: Hub personal org hook available
UUID generation is mocked to return an error
edge_case_tests.input: Hook called; UUID generator returns an error
edge_case_tests.expected: Hook returns non-nil error without executing any INSERT statement; transaction is rolled back
edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: insertCount := 0; tx := countingTx(func(){ insertCount++ }); mockUUID := func(){ return '', errors.New('uuid gen failed') }; err := hubOrgHookWithUUID(ctx, tx, 'user-402', 'uuidfail', 'u@test.com', mockUUID); assert err != nil AND insertCount == 0
